scholarships.title: Perimeter Institute PhD Residency Program Award
scholarships.funding_label: Doctoral funding package (university salary plus Perimeter top-up)

existing.description: Perimeter Institute awards a PhD Residency Program Award to doctoral students admitted to a partner Canadian university and supervised by a Perimeter faculty member, associate faculty member or senior researcher. The official page states that resident PhD students are financially supported through their home university, typically for four years or twelve academic terms, and that the Residency Award adds top-up funding up to $30,000 per year, calculated after fees and tuition, on a September to August academic year, until Term 12. Benefits also include a dedicated desk in a shared workspace, access to Perimeter facilities, a 50% discount at the on-site Black Hole Bistro, and a technology grant of up to $2,000.
eligibility: Apply to a PhD programme at a Perimeter partner university
Secure a supervisor who holds a Perimeter faculty, associate faculty or senior researcher appointment
Submit a separate Expression of Interest to the Perimeter PhD Residency Program Award
Upload the partner-university offer letter to the Expression of Interest application
Current PhD students may apply by indicating their university, term and supervisor
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must apply to a PhD programme at one of Perimeter's listed partner universities (Dalhousie, McMaster, University of Guelph, University of Toronto, University of Waterloo, Western, York) with a Perimeter-affiliated supervisor, and must submit a separate Expression of Interest to the Residency Award.
benefits: Top-up funding to $30,000 per year after fees and tuition until Term 12
Dedicated desk in a shared workspace at Perimeter Institute
Access to Perimeter Institute facilities, resources and scientific activities
50% discount at the on-site Black Hole Bistro
Technology grant of up to $2,000 for research-supporting technology
Mentorship from other PhD students and postdocs, and the opportunity to mentor an MSc student
Support and accommodations throughout the application process for applicants with disabilities
coverage: Home-university doctoral funding package covering the PhD, including fees and tuition
Perimeter top-up funding to a total of $30,000 per year after fees and tuition
Shared workspace desk and access to Perimeter facilities
requirements: One Expression of Interest listing up to five Perimeter Faculty or Senior Researchers
Separate application to the partner university's PhD programme
Expression of Interest submitted within one week of the partner-university application
documents: Expression of Interest to the PhD Residency Program Award
Partner-university offer letter (uploaded after offers are issued)
application_method: Apply to the partner university's PhD programme using that university's own process and deadlines
Submit the Perimeter Expression of Interest within one week of the university application
Upload the partner-university offer letter to the Expression of Interest when it arrives
existing.selection_notes: Applications are assessed against the research fit with a listed Perimeter supervisor; a formal residency offer cannot be made until the partner university has issued an offer letter.
existing.best_fit: Doctoral candidates in cosmology, mathematical physics, particle physics, quantum fields and strings, quantum foundations, quantum gravity, quantum information, quantum matter, strong gravity or computational physics who can secure a Perimeter-affiliated supervisor.
existing.notes: The Residency Award is additive: the official page states the top-up is calculated after fees and tuition, and that it builds on the university department's standard funding package. The award itself is therefore not published as a tuition payment, and fully_funded is recorded as false.
existing.duration: Up to Term 12 (typically four years / 12 academic terms)
existing.application_period: Expression of Interest submitted November to January, within one week of the partner-university application; partner universities issue offers February to March; Perimeter contacts selected students April to May; arrival in Waterloo August to September.

scholarships.title: Killam Fellowships Program (Fulbright Canada)
scholarships.official_source: Fulbright Canada, Foundation for Educational Exchange between Canada and the United States of America

existing.description: The Killam Fellowships Program, administered by Fulbright Canada, lets exceptional undergraduates from universities in Canada and the United States spend one semester or a full academic year as an exchange student in the other country. Fellows receive a cash award of US$6,000 per semester, or US$12,000 for a full academic year, plus a health benefit plan for American Fellows, a three-day orientation in Ottawa and a three-day spring seminar in Washington. All Fellows may apply for a mobility grant of up to CAD 800 for an educational field trip. Fellows either pay their home university fees as direct exchange students or pay host tuition as self-placed visiting students, so the award is a stipend rather than a tuition scholarship.
eligibility: Be an undergraduate student at a participating American or Canadian university
For the direct exchange route, be registered at a participating American university and plan to visit a participating Canadian university, or the equivalent for Canadians visiting the United States
Spend either one semester or a full academic year in the host country
Apply through the direct exchange institutional process or the open competition
Meet the academic criteria set by the home and host institutions
existing.eligibility_summary: Undergraduate students registered at one of the participating American or Canadian universities who are planning to spend a semester or a full academic year at a participating university in the other country. Direct exchange applicants must be registered at a participating university and plan to visit a participating university in the other country.
benefits: Cash award of US$6,000 per semester
Cash award of US$12,000 for a full academic year
Health benefit plan provided to all American Killam Fellows
Three-day orientation in Ottawa each fall and a three-day spring seminar in Washington
Mobility or in-country travel grant of up to CAD 800
Alumni enrichment opportunities including the Fulbright Canada Alumni Internship Program, the Killam Community Action Initiative and the Local Ambassador Program
coverage: Cash award of US$6,000 per semester or US$12,000 for a full academic year
Orientation in Ottawa and spring seminar in Washington
Mobility grant of up to CAD 800 for an educational field trip
requirements: Apply during the annual competition window, which opens on August 15
For the direct exchange route, apply by the internal deadline of the home institution
For the open competition, apply by January 31
Be registered at, and plan to study at, a participating university in the other country
Choose direct exchange or self-placed visiting student status, which determines who pays tuition
documents: Confirmation of registration at the home university
Host university nomination or exchange agreement for the direct exchange route
Academic records as required by the home and host institutions
Language evidence as required by the host institution
application_method: Apply through the direct exchange process at the home institution, or apply to the open competition
Submit by the home institution's internal deadline for the direct exchange, or by January 31 for the open competition
Use the Apply Now page on the Fulbright Canada site for the current application route
existing.selection_notes: The programme is described as providing an opportunity for exceptional undergraduate students. Fulbright Canada requires new Fellows to attend the fall orientation in Ottawa and offers a spring seminar in Washington.
existing.best_fit: High-achieving undergraduates at a participating Canadian or American partner university who can satisfy their home institution's tuition obligations and want one semester or a full year in the other country.
existing.notes: Tuition is not paid by the Killam award: direct exchange students register at and pay their home university, while self-placed visiting students pay host tuition. funding_amount is the full-academic-year figure; the one-semester award is US$6,000.
existing.duration: One semester or a full academic year
existing.application_period: The competition opens annually on August 15. Applications are for placement in Fall or Spring of the next school year, submitted by the internal deadline of the home institution for the direct exchange route, or by January 31 for the open competition.
existing.deadline_display: January 31 for the open competition; institution-set internal deadline for the direct exchange
